steps.title: File Jordan's signed raise letter
steps.context: Marcus Bell gave Jordan Reyes his pay increase letter on Thursday afternoon, and Jordan signed it the same day.

opener.speaker: mgr_bell
opener.line: Here's Jordan's signed raise letter, plus the unsigned draft. Do these go to payroll for his back pay, or what?

New rate: $24.50 per hour, effective Sunday, September 27
Approved: Dr. Helen Park, Director
Given to Jordan by Marcus Bell: Thursday, October 22
Employee signature: Jordan Reyes, Thursday, October 22

decisions.label: What to file, and where
decisions.prompt: What to file, and where

choices.text: Signed copy only, as a Document Record on his file
choices.feedback: Right. Signed letters go on the employee's Oracle file as Document Records, and only the final signed copy goes on. Payroll pays from the approved salary record, not from letters. Next time: name the record the way the type's description shows, so it's easy to find [SME: naming convention for compensation letters].

choices.text: Draft and signed copy, as Document Records on his file
choices.feedback: Only the final signed copy belongs on the file. A draft next to it invites questions about which terms are real. Next time: attach the signed final version and nothing else.

consequences.speaker: ec_menon
consequences.line: Jordan's file has two versions of his raise letter, and one isn't signed. Which one is real?
consequences.summary: An unsigned draft was filed next to Jordan's signed letter.

choices.text: Both copies to payroll by email, for his back pay
choices.feedback: Payroll pays from the approved salary record, so a letter in their inbox changes nothing, and Jordan's file is left without it. Next time: file the signed copy as a Document Record yourself.

consequences.speaker: pay_liu
consequences.line: I got Jordan's raise letter by email. We pay from the record, and his file still doesn't have the letter.

choices.text: Not filed by Friday
choices.feedback: The signed letter sat in your inbox, so Jordan's file has nothing to support his raise. Next time: file signed documents the day they arrive.

consequences.speaker: ec_menon
consequences.line: An audit sample pulled Jordan's raise, and there's no letter on his file.
consequences.summary: Jordan's raise had no signed letter on file.

decisions.label: Document Type
decisions.prompt: Document Type

choices.text: Compensation Letters

consequences.speaker: mgr_bell
consequences.line: I found Jordan's letter right where I expected it. Thanks for filing it so fast.
consequences.summary: Jordan's raise letter was filed under the right type.

choices.text: Performance Review
choices.feedback: Performance Review is for reviews and goal-setting documents. A pay increase letter is a Compensation Letters record, whatever led to the raise. Next time: read each type's description before you pick.

consequences.speaker: mgr_bell
consequences.line: I looked for Jordan's raise letter under compensation letters, and it wasn't there. It turned up under reviews.
consequences.summary: Jordan's raise letter was filed under the wrong document type.
consequences.task: Refile the letter as Compensation Letters.

choices.text: Performance and Discipline
choices.feedback: Performance and Discipline is for written, final, or termination level discipline and performance plans. A raise filed there puts a discipline label on Jordan's file. Next time: read each type's description before you pick.

consequences.speaker: emp_reyes
consequences.line: Marcus says my raise letter is filed under discipline. Is something wrong with my work?
consequences.summary: Jordan's raise letter was filed as a discipline document.
consequences.task: Refile the letter as Compensation Letters.

choices.text: Not filed
choices.feedback: Nothing was filed, so there was no type to choose. Next time: file signed documents the day they arrive.

decisions.label: Issued On
decisions.prompt: Issued On

choices.text: Sun Sep 27

consequences.speaker: ec_menon

consequences.summary: Jordan's document record shows the wrong issued date.

consequences.summary: The issued date on Jordan's letter is the upload date, not the day he received it.

choices.text: Not filed
choices.feedback: Nothing was filed, so there was no date to enter. Next time: file signed documents the day they arrive.

steps.title: A FERDC appointment form

steps.title: Noor will work from Illinois
steps.context: Noor Haddad starts Monday, on site at the Nashville office, and that is the work location on her Oracle assignment.

opener.speaker: mgr_bell
opener.line: Good news: Noor's moving to Illinois in January, and I told her she can work remotely from there. Anything you need from me?

steps.hint: Which rules follow a person to the state where they actually work, and who needs to hear about it before the move?

decisions.label: The move
decisions.prompt: Noor will work from Illinois starting in January. What do you do now?

choices.text: Get her work state and move date in writing, and send them to Ravi for review now
choices.feedback: A new work state can bring its own tax, unemployment, workers' compensation, and wage and leave rules, and the out of state review runs through your EC [SME]. Next time: flag a new work state the day you hear about it, well before the move.

choices.text: Wait until she moves in January, then have Ravi review it and update her location
choices.feedback: January is too late: state tax, workers' compensation, and pay rules need to be in place before she works there, and the review takes time. Next time: flag a new work state to your EC as soon as you hear about it.

consequences.speaker: ec_menon
consequences.line: Marcus mentioned Noor's Illinois move in passing. A new state needs review well before the move, and nobody told me.
consequences.summary: Noor's out of state move wasn't flagged for review.
consequences.task: Send Ravi Noor's work state and move date for the out of state review.

choices.text: Keep her location as Nashville, since her manager and department are based here
choices.feedback: Location tells payroll and benefits where she works, so Nashville would apply the wrong state's rules for tax, unemployment, and leave. Next time: the location is where the person actually works, not where the department sits.

consequences.speaker: pay_liu
consequences.line: If Noor works from Illinois with a Nashville location, payroll withholds no Illinois tax for her. We need to hear about a new state before her first check there.
consequences.summary: Noor's location would stay Nashville while she works in Illinois.
consequences.task: Flag Noor's Illinois move to Ravi and payroll.

decisions.label: Pay schedule
decisions.prompt: Marcus asks, "Her pay stays biweekly in Illinois, right?" What do you tell him?

choices.text: Payroll has to confirm it, since the state she works in sets pay frequency rules
choices.feedback: Pay frequency rules come from the state where the person works, so payroll compares Illinois's rule with her biweekly pay group before she moves [SME]. Next time: raise pay frequency with payroll for any new work state, before the offer or the move.

choices.text: Yes. Vanderbilt's pay calendars apply the same way in every state where we hire
choices.feedback: Each state sets its own pay frequency rules, and they follow where the person works, not where the department is. Next time: have payroll check a new state's rule before you promise anything.

consequences.speaker: mgr_bell
consequences.line: I told Noor nothing changes in Illinois. Now payroll says they have to check the state's pay rules first, and I look like I didn't know.
consequences.summary: Marcus promised Noor her pay wouldn't change before payroll checked Illinois rules.
consequences.task: Ask payroll to confirm Illinois pay frequency for Noor before January.

choices.text: Ask payroll to move her to monthly pay, so one check covers each month
choices.feedback: Monthly pay is for exempt staff, and Noor is non-exempt, so she stays hourly with a time card on a weekly or biweekly payroll. Next time: remember a move changes which state's rules apply, not the worker's pay group, so have payroll check the new state.

consequences.speaker: new_haddad
consequences.line: Marcus said I might switch to monthly pay when I move. I can't wait a whole month between paychecks.
consequences.summary: Noor was told she could move to monthly pay, which doesn't fit a non-exempt job.
consequences.task: Correct what Noor was told about her pay schedule.

decisions.label: In Oracle
decisions.prompt: When Noor starts working in Illinois, what do you change in Oracle?

choices.text: Her assignment's work location, to Illinois, effective the day she starts there
choices.feedback: Her assignment's location tells payroll and benefits where she works, and it changes on the day she starts working in Illinois. Next time: for a remote worker, set the location on the assignment, effective the real date.

choices.text: Her position's location, so the Nashville position moves to Illinois along with her
choices.feedback: Location doesn't sync from a position to an assignment, so her assignment would still say Nashville, and the position describes the on-site seat. Next time: for a remote worker, change the location on the assignment.

consequences.speaker: ec_menon
consequences.line: Changing the position won't move Noor to Illinois. Location doesn't sync to her assignment, and payroll reads the assignment.
consequences.summary: The plan changed Noor's position, not her assignment location.
consequences.task: Plan to change the location on Noor's assignment, effective her move date.

choices.text: Only her home address, since her work location stays with the Nashville office
choices.feedback: A home address isn't a work location. Payroll and benefits read the work location on her assignment, and it would still say Nashville. Next time: update the assignment location to where she actually works, effective the move.

consequences.speaker: ec_menon
consequences.line: A new home address won't tell payroll she works in Illinois. Her assignment's work location has to change when she moves.
consequences.summary: The plan changed only Noor's address, not her work location.
consequences.task: Plan to update Noor's assignment location, effective her move date.

choices.text: Nothing planned for the move
choices.feedback: Nothing was planned for the move. Next time: plan to update the assignment location for the day she starts working in Illinois.

steps.title: Illinois leave rules for Noor
steps.context: Noor Haddad asked Marcus about sick leave once she moves to Illinois in January. Marcus is passing the question to you.

opener.speaker: mgr_bell
opener.line: Noor wants to know if Illinois sick leave rules will apply to her. What should I tell her?

steps.hint: Whose rules apply to someone who works in another state, and who runs those programs?

decisions.prompt: What do you tell Marcus?

choices.text: They may. State leave laws follow where she works; send her question to Ravi
choices.feedback: Some states require sick or family leave beyond federal law, based on where the person works. Your part is routing the question and keeping her location right [SME]. Next time: send state leave questions to your EC before the move.

choices.text: Look up Illinois leave law yourself, then set up her sick leave in Oracle

choices.text: No. Her leave follows Tennessee rules, because her team is based in Nashville
choices.feedback: State leave laws follow where the person works, not where the department sits. Next time: send state leave questions to your EC, and keep the work location right.

steps.title: Sam's costing after his move
steps.context: Sam Okafor's transfer to the other school takes effect Sun Nov 8. His costing charges 100% to the department under program code 200, the front office team. Pay period 23, Oct 25 to Nov 7, is his last period with the department.

opener.speaker: emp_chen
opener.line: Once Sam moves on November 8, our account stops paying for him on its own, right? I just want to be sure.

steps.hint: When someone changes business units, does their costing reset or travel with them? And on which day does a pay period end?

decisions.label: Sam's costing
decisions.prompt: What do you do about Sam's department costing?

choices.text: End Date it before the move and tell the new school's HCM
choices.feedback: Costing follows a person across business units and doesn't reset, so the department's string would keep paying Sam. Ending it lets the new school's default or their own costing take over, and their HCM needs to know [SME: which HCM owns this step]. Next time: review costing on every transfer.

choices.text: Leave it; costing resets to the new school's default on Nov 8
choices.feedback: Costing doesn't reset on a business unit transfer. Sam's department string would follow him and keep charging your budget for work he does in the other school. Next time: review costing every time someone transfers.

consequences.speaker: emp_chen
consequences.line: I checked Sam's costing for November. It still points at our account after his move.
consequences.summary: Sam's department costing is set to follow him into the new school.
consequences.task: End Date Sam's department costing on Sat Nov 7.

choices.text: Delete his costing record so the default applies
choices.feedback: Delete Record removes the record completely, including the periods Sam already worked here, so his costing History no longer matches what was charged. Next time: End Date to stop costing; delete only a record that should never have existed.

consequences.speaker: emp_chen
consequences.line: Sam's costing History is gone. My reports for his past periods no longer match what was charged.
consequences.summary: Sam's costing record for past periods was deleted.
consequences.task: Restore Sam's costing record and End Date it on Sat Nov 7.

choices.text: Ask Tyler's team to switch the costing in the transfer
choices.feedback: The transfer moves Sam's job, not his costing, and central recruiting doesn't set costing. It follows him until an HCM reviews it in Costing for Persons. Next time: review costing yourself on every transfer, and tell the other HCM what you changed.

consequences.speaker: emp_chen
consequences.line: Tyler says transfers don't touch costing. Sam's string still points at our account after November 8.
consequences.summary: Sam's costing was left to central recruiting, so it will follow him into the new school.
consequences.task: End Date Sam's department costing on Sat Nov 7.

decisions.label: End Date search date
decisions.prompt: Which date do you search on to End Date Sam's costing?

choices.text: Sat Nov 7, the last day of period 23
choices.feedback: End Date searches on the last day of the last pay period the costing should apply. Period 23 ends Sat Nov 7, so the department pays for all of Sam's time with you and none after. Next time: End Date on a pay period end date.

choices.text: Fri Nov 6, his last workday with us
choices.feedback: Costing applies to the whole pay period, using what is in effect on the period end date. Ending it Fri Nov 6 leaves nothing in effect on Nov 7, so all of period 23 falls to the work unit default instead of program 200. Next time: End Date on the last day of the pay period, not the last workday.

consequences.speaker: emp_chen
consequences.line: Sam's costing ends November 6, so his whole last period will charge program 000 instead of the front office code.

consequences.speaker: emp_chen
consequences.line: Sam's costing runs to November 21, so we'd pay for his first two weeks at the new school.
consequences.summary: Sam's department costing was set to run into his first period in the new school.
consequences.task: Correct Sam's costing End Date to Sat Nov 7.

choices.text: Not entered
choices.feedback: Sam's costing was never ended, so it will follow him into the other school. Next time: finish a costing change the day you decide on it.

consequences.speaker: emp_chen
consequences.line: Sam's costing still points at our account after November 8. Can we fix it before his first check there?
consequences.summary: Sam's department costing was never ended.
consequences.task: End Date Sam's department costing on Sat Nov 7.

steps.title: Notice when a position is cut

steps.title: Checking everyone's costing at once

steps.title: Chase late approvals

steps.title: Cancel an approved day off
steps.context: Dana, in chat: "My Fri Nov 6 vacation day is already approved in Oracle. A site visit just moved to that day, so I'll be working."

opener.speaker: mgr_ortiz
opener.line: My Nov 6 day off is approved, but now I have to work that day. Can you just delete it?

steps.hint: How do you make an approved absence stop counting, without leaving a second record behind?

decisions.prompt: How do you cancel Dana's approved day off?

choices.text: Withdraw the absence in Oracle and check the withdrawal gets approved
choices.feedback: Right. An approved absence that won't happen is withdrawn, not deleted or offset. It may show Awaiting withdrawal approval until that's approved, then Withdrawn, and it stops counting. Next time: fix absences by editing or withdrawing the one on file.

choices.text: Add a second absence for Nov 6 with zero hours to cancel out the first
choices.feedback: A second absence doesn't cancel the first. It adds a duplicate, and her approved day still counts against her balance. Next time: withdraw the absence that shouldn't exist.

choices.text: Ask payroll to delete it, since an approved absence is locked to HCMs
choices.feedback: Payroll doesn't delete absences; it pays from what's recorded. An approved absence that won't happen is withdrawn in Oracle, which you or Dana can do. Next time: withdraw it yourself and track the withdrawal.

choices.text: Left on file
choices.feedback: The absence stayed on file, so the day still counts against her balance and shows her out on a day she worked. Next time: withdraw an absence that won't happen.
